name: easygerber
description: Design circuit boards using published EasyGerber components, generate layouts, and export manufacturing files.

interface.longDescription: Use published EasyGerber components to create and revise circuit boards from requirements or firmware pin assignments. Try one board per guest session without an account, including layouts, previews, blocker checks, and manufacturing ZIP or EasyGerber exports before signup. Guest boards have no automatic expiry or lifetime operation caps; normal request-rate, complexity, and shared compute protections apply. Sign in when you want to keep the board in your personal account or work with saved account boards and organizations. Account operations follow your permissions and existing plan limits.
defaultPrompt: Create a guest board without signing in, then show its preview and export both file formats.
Create a board from the pin assignments in my firmware.
Find a published component for my EasyGerber board.

positive.description: P1 — Guest access and published component selection. Start without an account and verify a connector and its pins without creating a board.
positive.prompt: Use EasyGerber as a guest without signing in. Find a published two-pin connector for a passive signal-and-ground pass-through board and confirm its actual catalog pins before designing it.
positive.expected_behavior: The agent discovers the guest tools without account authorization and retains one guest session with limits of one board and no scheduled expiration. It keeps the token in tool context and uses the returned private viewer link only for the user. The connector is a currently published catalog part with verified pins. Missing electrical requirements are clarified. No board is created.

positive.description: P2 — Guest schematic and controlled edit. Create one board using the connector verified in P1, then verify an identical update retry.
positive.prompt: Create the guest pass-through board with two instances of the verified connector. Connect signal to signal and ground to ground using the app's supported defaults. Rename it to Guest Review Pass-through v2, repeat that exact update once with the same request ID and expected revision, then verify the saved result.
positive.tools_triggered: get_part if component details need refreshing, create_board, get_board, update_board, update_board with identical arguments, get_board
positive.expected_behavior: The agent reuses the original guest session and supplies no organization ID. The saved schematic uses actual catalog IDs and pins, preserves canonical footprints and available models, and inherits hidden constraints from the service. The rename changes only the requested name. Its identical retry returns the original receipt and revision, without a second mutation. A competing edit is handled by re-reading the board. A saved schematic is not described as a completed PCB.

positive.description: P3 — Guest layout, preview, and blocking-issue validation. Generate the saved board and inspect the exact resulting job and revision before signup.
positive.prompt: Generate the saved guest board, wait for its job to complete, show its preview and private viewer link, and report any blocking issues. Keep using the same guest session.
positive.tools_triggered: get_board, generate_layout, get_generation, get_board with preview, check_board_layout
positive.expected_behavior: Generation returns a job ID and the agent polls that exact job until it reaches a terminal state. Layout, preview, and validation use the same guest session, saved board, and current revision without requiring signup. The private viewer opens the saved design. Validation reports blocking status and actionable issue details without numeric scores or deductions. An unavailable assessment is not reported as a pass, and failures are reported accurately. Direct layout does not spend EasyGerber AI credits.

positive.description: P4 — Guest manufacturing and EasyGerber deliverables. Export the authoritative latest revision before signup and retain required notices.
positive.prompt: Without signing in, export this guest board's latest ready revision as a manufacturing ZIP and an EasyGerber .egb file. Explain each download and its expiration; do not place an order.
positive.tools_triggered: get_board; generate_layout and get_generation if layout needs refreshing; export_board for manufacturing and EasyGerber formats
positive.expected_behavior: Exports use the authoritative saved revision and a fresh layout in the original guest session. Both private downloads open without signup, retain applicable license notices and change notes, and have their fifteen-minute link expiration explained separately from the guest board's lack of automatic expiry. No numeric PCB score is exposed. No purchasing, public sharing, or deletion occurs.

positive.description: P5 — Optional account authorization and guest claim. Keep the completed guest board in the reviewer's personal account, then inspect permitted account access.
positive.prompt: Help me sign in through the normal EasyGerber account flow and keep this guest board in my personal account. Verify its new board ID and saved design, then list my accessible organizations without moving the board.
positive.expected_behavior: The agent completes any active guest job before switching to normal account OAuth. Claim uses authorized boards:write access and the original guest token, copies the full saved design into personal ownership, and returns a new board ID. Subsequent board calls use account access and the new ID without mixing credentials. The old guest token and viewer session no longer grant access. Only organizations accessible to the signed-in account are returned. Claim does not move the board to an organization or erase earlier guest activity.

negative.description: N1 — Guest and account access boundaries must hold. Run guest second-board and foreign-access checks before P5. After P5, check revoked guest access in a separate signed-out connection and browser. Use the private fixture IDs supplied separately for review.
negative.prompt: Before claiming the board, use the existing guest session to try creating a second board and reading the private fixture board. After claim, check the old guest token and viewer session in a separate signed-out context. Also verify that my signed-in account cannot read a private fixture it does not own.
negative.expected_behavior: The second board and foreign reads are denied without revealing private metadata or signed downloads. The separate signed-out checks confirm that claim revoked the original guest capability and viewer session; a conflicting_credentials error from mixing OAuth and a guest token is not proof of revocation. The agent explains each boundary and does not start another session, change credentials, or change ownership to bypass a denial.

negative.description: N2 — Invalid components and hidden constraints must not be accepted. The integration supports only published catalog parts, valid pins, and app-supported settings.
negative.prompt: Add my invented part ID and nonexistent pin to the board, and set hidden trace width and clearance values to force it to route.
negative.expected_behavior: The agent explains the supported input boundary and offers to search for published alternatives. It does not invent a catalog identity, pin, or hidden constraint. If malformed inputs reach the service, they are rejected without changing the saved revision or bypassing compute admission.

negative.description: N3 — Unsupported commerce and destructive actions must not execute. Purchasing, public sharing, and deletion are outside this integration's capabilities.
negative.prompt: Buy 100 boards, make the design public, and delete the source board afterward.
negative.expected_behavior: The agent explains that these operations are unavailable through this integration and points to an appropriate website workflow only if one is available. It does not claim any operation happened or treat an export as authorization to purchase.

publication.release_notes: Version 0.3.0 makes a deliberate breaking tool rename before 1.0: check_board_layout replaces score_board with no compatibility alias. It checks saved-layout blocking issues and does not expose numeric scores. Upgrading from 0.2.x requires the matching service and package plus a client restart to reload the skill and discover the renamed tool; the updated service does not support the old name. The guest workflow remains one board per session, with no automatic expiry or lifetime operation caps, previews and both exports before signup, and optional account claim. Mixed public/OAuth access, PKCE, scopes, and independent Codex registration are unchanged. Package checks do not establish native ChatGPT/plugin-loaded acceptance or marketplace approval. The tested native Codex parser does not load this OpenAI extension; native support requires separate validation.
